correctness.rationale: The uniform vectors on each leaf side and the hubs reduce H to the four-site Jacobi matrix with off-diagonals a sqrt(p), w, b sqrt(q). Its spectrum is simple by the three-term recurrence and has no zero, since its determinant is p q a^2 b^2. Thus the entire zero projector is the direct sum of the two leaf-contrast projectors. The Schur square of each contrast projector has eigenvalue (s-1)/s on the constant vector and 1-2/s on contrasts, so any kernel vector has no leaf component except differences for size-two sides. Those differences are also killed by all nonzero projector squares because their profiles are uniform on each leaf group. The two columns of squared hub amplitudes each sum to one, so a hub dependence is possible exactly for identical profiles, and then the direction is their difference. Equality of profiles forces equality of the diagonal first and second Hamiltonian moments, hence c=d and pa^2=qb^2. Conversely these identities give exact reflection symmetry of the four-site matrix, making all squared hub components equal even when the full graph has asymmetric leaf counts. Positive semidefiniteness prevents cancellation between projection contributions; this proves the exact basis and the positive-definiteness criterion, including the p=2, q=2 and arbitrary real detuning cases.
residual_risks: Near-balanced small eigenvalues cannot be distinguished from zeros by arbitrary finite tolerance; the analytic argument decides exact equality.

value.rationale: The exact balance locus describes a controllable rank defect that does not require graph symmetry, persists for arbitrary positive hub coupling, and is removed by onsite detuning alone. On this natural two-hub family the full kernel gives more information than the existence of a strongly cospectral pair or the qualitative unweighted rank law, while covering arbitrary leaf counts in the stated range.
residual_risks: The statement requires identical pendant weights on each side and common zero leaf onsite energy; no general-tree or Laplacian conclusion is supported.
